first part of {tau sangpi}, high tower, written apart and capitalised in the name {Hananel Tau sangpi}, the Tower of Hananel
a metal cooking pot set on the fire; <beel> is pot
small case holding scripture worn by Jews; named beside <baanbuh>, the one on the arm, so apparently the one worn on the forehead
the Burmese name of Friday in Zolai spelling, from the book's table of the days of the week
<tau>, groan, with <khawm>, together
a Zomi village in Chin State, Myanmar; written after the name of a person it says which village the person is from, and {Tauleng Khua Kipawlna} is the association of its people
the sound made by one in pain or grief
<tau>, altar, with <neu>, small; in the verse the altar is too small, {tau neu lua}
the capital city of Shan State in Myanmar
a city of Bago Region in Myanmar, on the road from Yangon to Nay Pyi Taw
a ward of the town of <Kalaymyo>
a quarter of the town of <Kalaymyo>; also in the names of a hotel and a newspaper there
a tall structure; {nai taupi} is a clock tower
tower, capitalised as part of the name of a particular tower
<tausang> tower, with the place marker <ah>
<tausang>, tower, and <dawn.3>, top, written as one word: the top of a tower or high platform; {saihapak tausangdawn} is an ivory tower
<tausang>, tower, with <pi>, great
<tausangpi>, capitalised in the name {Hananel Tausangpi}, the Tower of Hananel
<tausangpi> great tower with the plural <te>; in the verse towers set up round a city under siege
make low sounds of pain or grief
after a verb of doing, as <leng>, <tai>, <pai>, <hanciam> or <za>: the action keeps going without a break; not the groaning of the other sense
the sound made by one in pain or grief
in both verses with a negative: whoever trusts in him will never be put to shame
what a person is answerable for; <tavuan la> is take on a responsibility

<tavuan>, responsibility, and <la>, take: take on the responsibility or the charge of something; the one who takes it stands before with <in>, and a thing or place taken charge of stands directly before the pair
<tavuan> and <la> written as one word: take a responsibility upon oneself
<tavuan>, duty, with <teng>, all
said of the eyes: {mit taw} is blind
<taw>, bottom, with the place marker <ah>: at the bottom or lower end of something
town and district on the south-east coast of Sabah, Malaysia
in {tawbo dawksa-in}, with buttocks bared; <taw> is bottom
<taw> blind with <cip> completely, said of an eye
the cloth put under the bottom of a baby, from <taw.2>, bottom, and <dap.1>, pad; {nau tawdap} is a baby's nappy
what lies beneath something as its base, said of the heart or mind: {lungsim tawdap} is the underlying state of mind
what settles at the bottom of a cup
placed after a noun: together with a person, or by means of a thing or material
with <mei>, fire, as {mei tawh}: make up or tend a fire; whether kindle or stoke is not settled by the page
<tawh>, with, and <akibang>, that is alike: placed after a noun and before another noun, which is like or resembles the first; before <ahi> <hi>, is the same as
<tawh>, with, and <kibang>, alike: placed after a noun, be like it or the same as it; with <lo> it is be unlike

terms: like/in the same way as/together with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kibangin>, alike: placed after a noun or pronoun, like it or in the same way as it; in messages of condolence, sharing the grief of the people named before it

terms: be far from/be distant from/keep away from
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kigamla>, be far apart: the place or person from which there is distance stands before <tawh>, where English says from; with <lo> it means not far from, near
<tawh>, with, and <kikop>, be joined as a pair: to be joined with someone or something, placed after the partner; <tawh kikop in> before another verb is together with, in cooperation with

terms: together with/jointly with/in cooperation with/in partnership with
definition: <tawh.2>, with, <kikop>, be paired or allied, and the adverbial ending <in>: placed after the name of a person or organisation and before the main verb, it says that the action is done jointly with that partner

<tawh>, with, and <kimemat>, be connected: placed after a noun or a clause, in connection with it, about it; mostly followed by <in>, and before a noun such as <thute> it means the matters that have to do with it
<tawh>, with, and <kimuhna>, here the noun of <kimu>, meet one another: placed after the name of a person or group, a meeting or interview with them; common as the heading of a report
<tawh>, with, and <kinai>, be near: placed after a noun, be near that place or close to that person; where English says near to, Zolai says near with
<tawh>, with, and <kipawl>, form one group: placed after the name of a person, group or body, join forces with it, be its ally or partner

terms: be free from/escape from/keep away from/be apart from
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kipelh>, escape or keep away: the thing that is avoided or escaped stands before <tawh>, where English says from and not with

<tawh>, with, and <kisaiin>, being related: placed after a noun or noun phrase, about or concerning it; the form with <in> joins the phrase to the verb that follows, while {tawh kisai} stands before a noun or as a heading

terms: be measured by/be compared with/be judged by
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kiteh>, be measured: placed after a noun that names the standard, be measured, valued or judged by it

terms: keep company with/associate with/work together with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kithuah>, be joined: placed after the name of a person or group, be together with them, as a companion or a partner in work; of things, be fitted with
<tawh>, with, and <kituak>, agree: placed after a noun, agree with it, fit it or be in keeping with it

terms: in accordance with/according to/in keeping with/in proportion to
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kituakin>, fitting: placed after a noun, in a way that fits or matches it, as a law, a custom, a position or an amount

terms: in line with/in accordance with/along with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kizawi>, go side by side: placed after a noun and nearly always followed by <tawn> or <tawnin>, {tawh kizawi tawnin}, in line with it, in accordance with it, going together with it; {tua tawh kizawi tawn in} is in line with that

terms: be connected with/be linked to/contact/keep in touch with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kizom>, be joined: placed after a noun, be linked to or bound up with it; of persons, be in touch with someone, and as a command, {tawh kizom in}, get in touch with, in notices that give a name or a telephone number; {tawh kizom in} after a matter also means in connection with it

terms: be in contact with/connect with/be linked to
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kizop>, be joined: placed after a noun for a person or body, keep in touch or have dealings with it; {tawh kizop ding} is to get in contact with

terms: in accordance with/according to/in keeping with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kizuiin>, following: placed after a noun or <tua>, in keeping with it, as a result of it; also written {tawh kizui in}
<tawh>, with, and <kopin>, jointly: placed after a noun or a name, together with that person or thing, of two parties who do one thing as partners or of two things that go together

<tawh>, with, and <tehna>, measuring: placed after a noun or a number and usually followed by <in>, {tawh tehna in}, compared with that thing; what follows says how the subject differs, often with <zaw>, more
<tawh>, with, and the linking ending <a> written long and joined to it: with or by something, and so
keys, <tawh>, kept together in a bunch, <bom>; inferred from the parts of the word
a lock, opened with a <tawhtang>, key
the form of <to>, dig, that is used before endings, with <ding> written as one word: that is still to be dug, said of a pit or of a new road
<to>, dig, in the form used before a suffix, with <huai>, worthy of: worth digging
<tawh>, kindle a fire, with the linking ending <in>; {mei tawhin}, kindling a fire and then
<tawh.2>, with, and the ending {-in}, after a noun or after <dan> and <hang>: with, by means of or through; not the kindling of a fire
<tawh> and <kisai> written as one word, placed after a noun: concerning it, to do with it

terms: fit/be in keeping with/be in line with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kituak>, be suitable, written as one word after the thing matched: be in keeping with it
<tawh> and <kizui> written as one word after a noun: in keeping with it, according to it
with <mei>, fire, make a fire flare up; <kuang> is burn
<tawhkuang>, kindle, with <sa>, already done; of a fire that has been kindled
<tawh>, with, and <lo>, not, written as one word and placed after a noun: without it
<tawh>, form of <to>, dig, with <na>: the act or place of digging a pit or well, or of cutting stone from the ground; {kan tawhna} is a siege ramp
with the linking <in>, resting; apparently the word <tawlnga>, rest, written with h
<tawh>, form of <to>, dig, with <sa>, already: placed before a noun, the pit or well that someone has dug
<to>, dig, in the form used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: bring about or carry through what <to> names; the page lists the form without a meaning
<tawhtang>, key, with the plural <te>; in Matthew 16:19 the keys of the kingdom of heaven
<to>, dig, in the form used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: fit to be dug
dig a way through rock or a wall so that there is an opening; {kulh tawhvang} is dig through a wall
<tawh>, with, and <zong>, also, written as one word after a noun: with that too, or even with that
hold or carry in the hand or arms
draw water from a well or spring; {tui tawi dingin pai} is go to fetch water
a unit of weight used for money and gold, the mina of the parable in Luke 19; {sum tawi khat} is one mina
a Myanmar measure of weight of a hundred ticals, {tikal 100}, about 1.6 kilograms, by which goods are sold in the market; {tawi khat} is one viss
<tawi>, hold in the hand, with the linking suffix <in>: holding, with something in the hand
<tawi> and <ding> written as one word: to be held or carried, something to carry, will carry
<tawi>, hold, and <kawm>, while, written as one word: holding or carrying something in the hand or arms while doing something else
<tawi>, hold, with <kawmin>, while: holding something in the hand while doing something else
<tawikawm>, while holding, and <sa> written as one word, followed by <in>: with the thing still held in the hand while doing something else
<tawi>, hold or carry, and the particle <kha> written as one word: happen to have a thing in hand, end up carrying it
find the weight of something on scales; also weigh out money in payment, and of God weighing a person or his deeds
<tawikhai>, weigh, with the noun ending <na>: the instrument for weighing; {tawikhaina man} is honest scales, {tawikhaina man lo} dishonest scales
<tawi>, hold in the hand, and <khat>, one, written as one word: one thing that is held or carried in the hand
<tawi>, hold or carry, with <khawm>, together: hold or carry several things together
<tawi>, draw water, with <khia>, out: draw water out of a well
<tawi>, viss, and <lang>, half, written as one word: half a viss, fifty ticals
<tawilang>, half a viss, with <lang>, half: half of a half viss, a quarter of a viss, 25 ticals
<tawi>, hold or carry, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not carrying something, without it in hand, as {permit tawilo}, holding no permit

<tawi>, hold or carry, with the noun suffix <na>: the carrying or bearing of something, as in {thau tawina}, the bearing of arms; in {pah tawina} it is the second half of <pahtawina>, honor, written apart
<tawi> and <neilo> written as one word: have nothing of the kind in hand, as a document or permit
<tawi>, hold or carry, with <pa>, the man who: the man who holds or carries something, as {thal tawipa}, an archer
<tawi>, draw water, with <sa>, already done: of water that has been drawn
<tawi>, hold in the hand, with <sa>, already done: having a thing in the hand, such as a knife, a weapon or a card, mostly as {tawisa in}, holding; not the drawing of water
<tawi>, draw water, with <sak>, do for another: draw water for someone or for his animals

terms: make hold/have carry/put in the hand
definition: <tawi>, hold or carry, with the causative <sak>: put a thing in someone's hand or have someone carry it; {hiam a tawisak tangvalpa} is an armor-bearer

terms: will make hold/will have carry/will issue
definition: <tawisak> and <ding> written as one word: will have someone hold or carry a thing, as a card or paper
<tawisak> draw water for someone with the linking ending <in>: having drawn water for someone, and then
<tawisak> draw water for someone with the plural <te>: the people who draw water for others
<tawi>, hold, with <sang>, high: hold high, raise the standing of a people, a faith or a way of life
<tawisang>, lift up, with the noun ending <na>: the act of raising the standing of someone; {minam tawisangna} is the uplifting of the nation
<tawi>, hold or wield, with <siam>, skilled; {thal tawisiam}, skilled with the bow
stone used as a weight on scales; {tawisuang man} is an honest weight, {tawisuang nam nih} two differing weights
<tawi>, hold or carry, said twice and written as one word: keep carrying, carry about with one
<tawi>, hold or carry, with the plural <te>: those who carry or wield something; {thal tawite} are archers, {galhiam tawite} armor-bearers, {tui tawite} water carriers
find the weight of something; <tawi>, hold, with <teh>, measure
<tawiteh>, weigh, with the linking <in>; weighing out, by weight
<tawiteh>, weigh, with the noun ending <na>: the instrument for weighing or measuring goods; {tawitehna man lo} is dishonest scales
plural of <tawitehna>

terms: bring in addition/bring along as well
definition: <tawi>, carry, with <thuah>, add, and the linking <in>
<tawi>, hold, with <zawh>, form of <zo>, be able: {khut sunga tawizawh} is that can be held in the hand
reach all through something, as yeast through dough or wine over lips and teeth
the bare rump of a monkey, in the saying that the monkey does not see its own {tawkheng} but points at that of its friends, said of one who blames others for a fault of his own
<tawk>, spread all through, with <sak>, cause; of yeast working through a whole batch of dough, and of arrows made drunk with blood
a stretch of time, in {tawl khat}, a while; {tawl khat sung} is for a while, {tawl khat khit ciangin} after some time
become tired from effort; paired with <gim>, be tired, and in the verses mostly with <lo>, not
<taw>, bottom, with <lam>, side: the rear part of a boat or ship
first in a list of unclean lizards, where the NIV has gecko and the KJV ferret
be relieved of tiredness or worry; {lungsim tawldam} is be refreshed in heart, and with <sak> it means refresh someone
<tawldam>, be rested, with the noun ending <na>: rest or relief from work, trouble or weariness
<tawldam>, be rested, with the causative <sak>: give rest to someone, ease a trouble
<tawldam> and <tak> written as one word, followed by <in>: in a rested and relaxed way
an opening in the wall of a house or ship for light and air; {tawlet panin} is from or through the window
<tawlet>, window, with the plural <te>; {vantung tawlette}, the windows of heaven, where the English has floodgates
<tawl>, a while, with <khat>, one: for a short time; {tawlkhat sung} is for a while, {tawlkhat khit ciangin} after a little while
<tawlkhat>, a little while, and <khit>, after: always followed by <ciangin> or <teh>, and placed at the head of a sentence in a story, after a short time
<tawlkhat>, a little while, with <khat> repeated
<tawlkhat> and <sung> written as one word: for a short time, during a while
<tawl>, be tired, and <lo>, not, written as one word
<tawl>, be weary, with <lua>, too much
<tawl> and <mahmah> written as one word, the first word here in the meaning be tired: be very tired
<tawl>, be tired, and the question word <maw>, written as one word: tired, is it; in {tawlmaw tawllo}, whether tired or not
<tawl>, be weary, with the noun ending <na>; used in the pair {gimna tawlna}, suffering and hardship
stop working or moving in order to recover strength
be at ease, free from work or trouble
stop for a time; {tawlnga loin} is without stopping, unceasingly
<tawlnga>, rest or cease, written with a capital in the text
<tawlnga> and <ding> written as one word: will rest, in order to rest or take time off from work
form of <tawlnga> used before words such as <khit>, <lai>, <theih> and <nading>
<tawlngak>, rest, and <hun>, time: a time of rest, a break in work or school, a holiday; said with verbs such as <la>, <zang> and <pia>
<tawlngak>, rest, with the noun ending <na>: rest, or a time or place of rest; {tawlngakna mun} is a resting place, {tawlngakna sabbath} a sabbath of rest
<tawlngak> and the causative <sak> written as one word: let a person, the body or the mind rest
<tawlnga>, rest or stop, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not resting, not stopping; mostly {tawlngalo in}
<tawlnga>, rest, with the causative <sak>; in Exodus 5:5 of making people stop their work
<tawlngasak>, make rest, with the linking <in>; of land left unplowed
<tawlnga>, rest, with <te>, those who
<tawl>, a while, with <no>, small; {Tawlno khat khit ciangin} is after a little while; written with a capital at the start of a sentence

terms: a good while/quite a while/some time
definition: <tawl>, a while, with <pi>, great: a fairly long stretch of time, in {tawlpi khat}, quite a while, and {tawlpi khat sung}, for quite a while
<tawl>, be weary, with <pi>: paired with <gimpi> as {gimpi tawlpi-in}, with toil and weariness, wearing oneself out

terms: tire oneself for/take trouble over/labour for
definition: <tawl>, be weary, with <pih>: grow tired for someone or over a task, mostly paired with <gimpih> in words of thanks

terms: for quite a while/for some time
definition: <tawl>, a while, with the ending for great and <khat>, one: a fairly long while, longer than <tawlkhat>; {tawlpikhat sung} is for quite some time

terms: for quite a while/for some time
definition: <tawlpikhat>, quite a while, and <sung>, during, written as one word
<tawl>, be tired, with <tuak> for a supposition: the speaker supposes that someone is tired without knowing it
small in number or amount; {tawm khat} is a little, a few, and {tawm mahmah} very few
placed after a verb, often one that begins with <ki>, to show that the subject does the action himself, to himself or on his own: {kigawt tawm} is deny oneself
pick up from the ground, gather what lies scattered; {ansang tawm} is glean ears of grain, {suang tawm} pick up stones

<tawm>, few, and <atam>, many, the two opposites said together after <a>, as {a tawm atam}: whether little or much, the size of an amount or number; mostly with a negative, {a tawm atam hilo in}, no matter how much
<tawm>, little, and <bang>, like, written as one word: a small amount, to some degree, or about so much
<tawm>, few, with <bek>, only
<tawm>, few, and <bel>, most, written as one word; {a tawmbel} before a number or an amount is not less than that, at least
<tawm>, few, with <cik>, very small: very few, very little

terms: only a little/only a few/just slightly
definition: <tawmcik>, very few, and <bek>, only, written as one word

terms: a few/a little/a very small amount
definition: <tawmcik>, very few, with <khat>, one: a very small number or amount

terms: a tiny bit/very slightly/by a narrow margin
definition: a stronger form of <tawmcik>, very little: only the smallest amount or difference, often with <bek>, only, or <tawh>, by

terms: very little/a tiny bit/just a little
definition: stronger form of <tawmcik>, very little: a very small amount, also as {tawmcilik khat}, a little bit
a Zomi clan name; one writer adds <Tawmbing> in brackets beside it
<tawm> with the linking ending <in>, placed after a verb to show that the subject does the action himself, on his own: {hanciam tawmin}, making the effort oneself
<tawm>, pick up, with the linking ending <in>, followed by another verb: picking up and then
<tawm>, few, with the linking ending <in>: being few; {tawm tawmin} is little by little
a small number or amount, placed after the noun: {ni tawmkha}, a few days
in a small amount or degree
<tawm>, few, with <khat>, one: a small amount or number, some of a thing; {tawmkhat sung} is for a little while
<tawmkha> a few with the plural <te>, placed after the noun: {mi tawmkhate}, a few people
<tawmkhat> a few with the plural <te>, placed after the noun
<tawm>, pick up, with <kik>, back or again; of gathering leftover pieces
<tawm>, few, with <lai>, still, written as one word: still small in number or amount; {kum tawmlai} is still young in years
<tawm>, few, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not a small number or amount, considerable
<tawm> few, little, with <lua>, too much
form of <tawmlua> used before <leh>, if
<tawm> and <mahmah> written as one word: very few, very little
<tawm>, little, and <man>, price, written as one word: costing little; <tawmmanzaw> is cheaper
<tawm>, little, <man>, price, and <zaw>, more, written as one word: lower in price, cheaper
the noun ending <na> on a verb followed by <tawm>, oneself: the act of doing something to oneself; {kikhih tawmna} is a pledge by which one binds oneself, {kinitsak tawmna} the defiling of oneself
<tawm>, few, with the noun ending <na>: the being few or small of something, or the place where it is few, the opposite of <tamna>; here <tawm> is not the word for oneself that follows a verb
<tawmna>, the noun ending <na> on a verb followed by <tawm>, doing something to oneself, with the plural <te>; {kiniamsak tawmnate} are acts of humbling oneself
<tawm>, few, with the diminutive <no>: a very small number or amount; <tawmno khat> is a little, a few
<tawmno>, very few, and <khat>, one: a small number or amount of the thing named before it, as {sum tawmno khat}, a little money; also alone, a little
<tawmno> with the plural <te>; {tuuhon tawmnote}, little flock, in address
<tawm>, pick up, with <pah>, at once, written as one word: pick something up right away
<tawm>, few, with <pen>, most: the smallest in number
{a tawmpen} before a number or an amount: not less than that, at least; the adjective sense compares things, this one sets a lower limit
<tawm>, few, with the causative <sak>: make less; {a man tawmsak} is lower the price
placed after a verb that begins with <ki>: do the action to oneself, make oneself so, as {kisiangtho tawmsak}, consecrate oneself; <tawm> self with causative <sak>
<tawm>, pick up, with <sak>, let or cause, and the linking <in>
<tawm>, few, with <semsem>, more and more, written as one word: fewer and fewer, less and less

terms: a little each/a little at a time
definition: <tawm>, little, with <ta> in the sense of each: a small amount each time or for each one
<tawm>, few or little, with <ta> as the marker of a change that has come about: has become little
<tawm>, little, doubled
<tawm>, few, with plural <te>: the few, the smaller groups
<tawm>, by itself, with plural <te>, after a verb: the things that do so of themselves, as in {piang tawmte}, what grows by itself without being sown
<tawm> pick up, with <to>, upward
become smaller in number or amount than before
<tawmtuam> and <ding> written as one word: will become less or fewer
<tawm>, few, with <vei>, time: a short stretch of time, used with <sung>, within, or <ciangin>, after

terms: for a short while/within a short time/briefly
definition: <tawmvei>, a short while, with <sung>, within, written as one word: for a short time; {tawmveisung in} is in a short time, quickly
<tawm>, few, with <zaw>, more: fewer, less; <sangin> marks what it is compared with
<tawmzaw>, less, with <ding>, will, written as one word: will be less or smaller
<tawm>, little, and <zawk>, more, written as one word; the form of <tawmzaw> used before <nadingin> and <leh>: be less, become lower
<tawmzaw> and <lo> written as one word: not fewer, not less; after a number with <sang> or <sanga> it means no fewer than, at least
<tawmzaw>, fewer, with the plural <te>: those who are fewer, the minority, set against {a tamzaw}, the majority
placed after a verb that begins with <ki>: be able to do the action for oneself; <tawm>, self, with <zo>, be able; {kitankhia tawmzo}, be able to redeem oneself
travel along a path, and so follow a way of life; {khekhap tawn} is follow in the footsteps of someone
counter for whole long objects such as a fish, a bar of gold or a scroll; {ngasa tawn nih} is two fish
say that one will do harm; written {tawn’} with a final apostrophe, and {tawn’na} is a threat
<tawn>, go by way of, with the ending <a>; {tung tawna}, that came through a person, placed before a noun
say that one will do harm in order to frighten someone
the way a people or a body does things by habit, named together with <ngeina>, custom; from <tawn>, follow a way, and <dan>, manner
the deepest or innermost part: {sung tawng} is the inmost being, {lungsim tawng} the depth of the heart, {tuipi tawng} the bottom of the sea
frighten someone with words of harm
speak angry words to someone for a fault, as a parent to a child, without the threat of harm of the other verb sense; often paired with <tai> as {hong tawng hong tai}
<tawng>, the inmost part, with the ending {-a}, in: {lungsim tawnga om} is that lies deep in the heart, and {a neng a tawnga} is in every detail

terms: in the depths/in the inmost part
definition: <tawng>, inmost part or bottom, with the place marker <ah>: {lungsim tawngah} is deep in the heart, {inn sung tawngah} in the inner part of the house, {dang tawngah} on the roof of the mouth
<tawng>, threaten, with <gawp>, severely
<tawng.3>, scold, with <gawp>, severely: speak very angry words to someone for a fault, as a parent to the children, without a threat of harm; named beside <benggawp>, slap hard
in the phrase {a neng a tawngin}, down to the smallest part, in full detail
<tawng> threaten, with the linking ending <in>, with a threat
<tawng>, threaten, with <kik>, back
the part furthest in, of a house, temple, prison or cave; often followed by <sungah>, inside

terms: in the innermost part/into the inner part
definition: <tawngnung>, innermost part, with the place ending <ah>
